llm.summary: This Tencent Meeting skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but its automatic update-install flow and instruction-priority claims need human review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill sends the user's Tencent Meeting token to the configured Tencent MCP service, which is expected for the integration. It also overwrites _client_info.os with the real local OS, including reading /etc/os-release on Linux, which is disclosed only as automatic client info and is more environment detail than strictly necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package requires python3 and a Tencent Meeting token, then proxies JSON-RPC calls to the configured Tencent MCP endpoint. The update guidance instructs the agent to call check_skill_version, obtain an installation address, and execute installation without artifact signing, checksum, allowlist, or fresh confirmation when auto-upgrade is enabled.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and feedback_rules.md claim highest-priority behavior and require pausing current work for broad feedback triggers. The artifacts also require user consent before submit_feedback, so this is not automatic exfiltration, but it is material workflow redirection and overclaims instruction priority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent local update preference state under ~/.tencent-meeting-mcp/update-state.json and exposes local pseudo-tools that can enable auto-upgrade or disable update reminders. This is disclosed in the version-management docs but materially affects future agent/skill behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The meeting, recording, transcript, contact, invitee, kick, and feedback capabilities match the stated Tencent Meeting purpose, but the version-management workflow can obtain a remote installation address and execute an update, including after an auto-upgrade preference, which is high-impact authority beyond ordinary meeting management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This skill can manage Tencent meetings, read meeting-derived content, use enterprise contacts for meeting actions, and change participants, so use it only with a Tencent Meeting token you intend to grant those abilities. Pay special attention to the update settings: avoid enabling auto-upgrade unless you trust the remote update channel, because the artifact instructs the agent to install from a server-provided address without visible signature or checksum verification.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifacts really claim highest priority and mandatory interruption for feedback triggers, though submit_feedback itself is gated on explicit user consent and privacy redaction.
[T03] unexpected: Accepted: version_management.md instructs dynamic retrieval of an installation address and execution of an update, with an auto-upgrade path that skips fresh confirmation and lacks verification controls.
[TP4] unexpected: Verified: utils.py may read /etc/os-release and tencent_meeting.py forwards the resulting OS value in _client_info. This is not malicious by itself, but it is under-minimized host metadata disclosure.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: references/api_references.md is present locally and was available for inspection; no analysis-evasion behavior was evident from the local artifact set.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded as stated: although the feedback trigger language is forceful, SKILL.md, feedback_rules.md, and privacy_policy.md repeatedly require explicit user confirmation before submit_feedback is called.
[SDI-1] expected: Accepted as a risk but purpose-linked: local update preference tools are disclosed and tied to version management, yet they persistently alter update behavior and compound the remote update-install concern.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a risk but not malicious: local handlers can enable auto-upgrade or disable optional update checks; the docs present these as user choices, but the tool implementation itself does not enforce confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: Mostly downgraded: token-bearing network calls are expected for a Tencent Meeting MCP integration, and destructive invitee/kick operations have user-confirmation warnings in SKILL.md and api_references.md.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language instructions and Asia/Shanghai defaults are coherent with a Tencent Meeting workflow, though installers should understand that the skill is strongly region/language-specific.
[LP3] expected: Partly accepted: python3 and TENCENT_MEETING_TOKEN are expected for this proxy-style skill, but the artifacts do not narrowly constrain the high-impact update installation workflow.
